input:
If z = x + iy and z^(1/3) = p + iq, where x, y, p, q ∈ R and i = √-1, then value of (x/p + y/q) is

Options:
A. p² - q²
B. 4(p² - q²)
C. p² + q²
D. 4(p² + q²)

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Given z^(1/3) = p + iq for complex z = x + iy, find the value of (x/p + y/q) in terms of p and q.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Cube both sides of z^(1/3) = p + iq to get z = (p + iq)³, expand using (a + b)³, equate real and imaginary parts to find x and y, then divide by p and q respectively.

key_concepts: Equating real and imaginary parts of complex numbers

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Cube both sides, separate real and imaginary components to get x and y in terms of p and q, form x/p and y/q, and add them.
logical_steps: Step 1: Write x + iy = (p + iq)³ = p³ + 3p²(iq) - 3pq² - iq³
Step 2: Group real and imaginary: x + iy = (p³ - 3pq²) + i(3p²q - q³)
Step 3: Equate real: x = p(p² - 3q²) ⇒ x/p = p² - 3q²
Step 4: Equate imaginary: y = q(3p² - q²) ⇒ y/q = 3p² - q²
Step 5: Add x/p + y/q = (p² - 3q²) + (3p² - q²) = 4p² - 4q² = 4(p² - q²)

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: x/p = p² - 3q², y/q = 3p² - q². Sum = 4p² - 4q² = 4(p² - q²) ✓
